documents.title: Problem with function Close()
documents.summary: The Close() function in pool.go freezes because len(p.idleResources) != len(p.allResources) after removing idle resources. The issue occurs when p.destructWG.Wait() is called without ensuring all resources in p.allResources are accounted for. A fix is proposed: after removing idle resources, iterate over p.allResources and remove each resource while calling p.destructWG.Done() for each, ensuring all destruct operations are properly tracked and completed.

documents.title: Non-blocking version of Acquire
documents.summary: Proposes adding a non-blocking version of `Acquire` to the API, named `TryAcquire`, `AcquireNow`, or `AquireOrFail`, to fail immediately if no resources are available and no headroom exists for new construction. Current workarounds using short-lived contexts are deemed clunky and risky due to potential cancellation of valid resource construction. The use case is a scheduler that acts on available resources. The author offers to submit a pull request if the feature is accepted.

documents.title: Fix several memory leaks
documents.summary: Fixes memory leaks caused by modifying slice lengths without removing elements from the backing array, leading to connections remaining in memory after closure. The issue was reproduced with a self-contained program at https://github.com/atombender/pgx-leak; on a machine dated 2021-11-11, heap usage rose to 3741 MB before the fix and dropped to 0 MB afterward. The fix ensures GC can reclaim memory when connections are closed.

documents.title: Fix Acquire lock issue if nil is passed as context
documents.summary: Panic immediately if nil is passed as the ctx argument in Acquire. The issue was observed during a test case where a context was omitted, causing the test to hang indefinitely. The problem is linked to issue #1, pull request #12, and this fix.

documents.title: TryAcquire will be blocked when construct resource failed
documents.summary: TryAcquire will be blocked for 5 seconds when constructing a network resource fails, as DialTimeout blocks for 5 seconds during a failed TCP connection attempt to addr. The block occurs when the network is unavailable and the constructor function returns an error.

documents.title: No wait try acquire
ctx done
The function Acquire does not return immediately，when ctx Done()
documents.summary: The Acquire function in pool.go does not return immediately when ctx.Done() is called due to a lock attempt before returning. If maxSize is exceeded and no resources are released, the function waits for a resource to be freed, causing unnecessary locking. The author suggests that the Stat field may not be useful in practice, as it increases locking complexity and is likely handled by monitoring systems. The issue occurs in pool.go and involves ctx.Done(), waitChan, p.canceledAcquireCount, and p.cond.L.

documents.title: Use atomic operations to avoid locking as much as possible
documents.summary: Used atomic operations to reduce locking in a code change related to GitHub issue https://github.com/jackc/puddle/issues/17. Performance showed minimal difference when looping 10,000 times, but with 100,000 loops, 91,568 rows were output on the new branch versus 86,648 rows on master, indicating slightly better performance in the implementation.

documents.title: Generics support
documents.summary: Go 1.18, released with generics support, improves library usage by eliminating the need for type casting. The feature requires changes and breaks backward compatibility, necessitating a version 2 upgrade. A backward compatibility solution was found and implemented in a PR.

documents.title: Fix deadlock race when acquire is cancelled
documents.summary: Fixes a deadlock race when acquire is cancelled by scheduling the second goroutine before locking, ensuring one of the two can release the lock and prevent deadlock when the waiter goroutine is signaled before the canceledAcquireCount guard runs.

documents.title: Move main logic to  package and use generics for API with backwards compatibility
documents.summary: Moved main logic to a package and updated the API to use generics while maintaining backwards compatibility through type aliases for `any` types and wrapper functions. The change closes issue #19.

documents.title: Create resources in the background in Acquire
documents.summary: Modifies Acquire to create resources asynchronously when the context is cancelled; constructors that ignore cancellation continue creating resources even if Acquire is cancelled. Fixes GitHub issue https://github.com/jackc/pgx/issues/1287.

documents.title: Fix race with background Acquire creation
Backport background acquire to v1
documents.summary: Backports pull requests #21 and #22 to the v1 branch.

documents.title: Replace conditional variable with semaphore
documents.summary: Replaced conditional variable with semaphore in `pgxpool.Pool.Acquire()` to resolve long latency during load tests with CPU-heavy workloads and request cancellations. The change eliminates adapter goroutines that caused blocking and feedback loops under cancellation. Benchmarks show reduced latency: `BenchmarkAcquire_MultipleCancelled` improved from 334μs to 149μs, and `BenchmarkAcquire_MultipleCancelledWithCPULoad` from 1.48ms to 117μs. The fix also prevents goroutine leaks and modifies `AcquireAllIdle` to use a generational stack for thread-safe resource management.

documents.title: Call to Close() hangs
documents.summary: A Go program using pgxpool fails to terminate properly when interrupted with ctrl+C, hanging on `db.Close()` and specifically on `p.destructWG.Wait()`. The issue is reliable and reproducible, especially when ctrl+C is pressed early in the program's execution. The program uses a loop that continuously executes `db.Exec` with a 0.2-second sleep, and the hang occurs during cleanup. The issue is reported on Linux with Go 1.19. No specific fix or cause is provided.

documents.title: Recent commit in puddle requires 1.19 while pgx is still on 1.18
documents.summary: A recent commit in puddle (86ffb019e1946f3158391f64e8d944787bdbc2b3) requires Go 1.19, but pgx still requires Go 1.18. pgx uses a replace directive to pull puddle/v2, causing build failures on Go 1.18 due to missing atomic.Int64. The issue requests support for Go 1.18 and 1.19, citing Google's policy and infra team requirements. A pgx version bump (5.0.4) was previously made, and this issue ensures it was not accidental.

documents.title: question: How to automatically delete outdated resources?
documents.summary: Asks how to automatically delete outdated resources created more than a certain number of minutes ago, specifically for AWS, databases, and Google Cloud Platform credentials. Considers destroying resources on error but warns it may drain the resource pool during genuine errors. Currently uses a manual check to detect and destroy resources older than a threshold. No specific time, resource names, or identifiers are provided.

documents.title: update: example usage
documents.summary: The example usage in the documentation was outdated and has been updated to reflect the current way of using the library.

documents.title: Add histogram support for acquire duration
documents.summary: Adds optional histogram support for acquire duration, inspired by the prom grpc middleware; user can enable it via options; author requests feedback on the PR and asks if there is no intention to add such histogram support.

documents.title: maintain lastUsedTime so clients can use it as a factor in idle and …
documents.summary: Maintain lastUsedTime to allow clients to use it as a factor in idle and health check logic.

documents.title: Add ability to set arbitrary external acquire duration observer
documents.summary: Adds the ability to set an arbitrary external acquire duration observer as a rework of PR #29. No dependencies are added or updated. Changes do not break backward compatibility; the observer is optional and must be explicitly set by users. The author states they see no other way to measure acquire duration correctly and will not submit additional PRs unless this one is considered.

documents.title: Fix documentation of NewPool
Undefined: atomic.Int64
documents.summary: Error "undefined: atomic.Int64" occurs when running "make run" in github.com/jackc/puddle/v20v2.2.1/pool.go at line 142. The issue is reported on Go 1.22 running on an Ubuntu 23.10 VM. The user requests assistance to resolve the undefined identifier.

documents.title: Question: are you ok if we add the possibility to resize the max pool size?
documents.summary: Asks if the AI is open to a pull request that adds the ability to resize the max pool size on the fly. The requester offers to create the pull request if approved.

documents.title: feat(pool): Add EmptyAcquireWaitTime stats
documents.summary: Adds EmptyAcquireWaitTime statistics to measure the time taken for resource acquisition when the pool is empty and must wait or construct a new resource.

documents.title: Stop importing nanotime from runtime via linkname
documents.summary: Go authors locked down linkname usage; Puddle removes reliance on linkname to import nanotime using a performance-neutral trick. The approach was previously used in otter v2 to optimize time operations due to `time.Now` being slow. Benchmark results show `time.Since` and `nanotime` are functionally equivalent, with `nanotime` performing at 1.920 ns/op versus 34.51 ns/op for `time.Now`. The change has minimal performance impact.

documents.title: Remove reliance on package unsafe
documents.summary: Removes reliance on the `unsafe` package by replacing `log2Int` in `log.go` with `math/bits.Len64`. The function is unexported and currently used only in `pool.go` at line 551. The replacement uses `bits.Len64(val) - 1` with range checking and casting to ensure correctness. The change is proposed because Go's standard library provides a high-performance alternative. An example implementation and a playground link are provided.

documents.title: Application Hangs on `defer p.destructWG.Wait()` in Docker Environment
documents.summary: Application hangs on `defer p.destructWG.Wait()` when run in a Docker container using `golang:1.22-alpine` on Windows via Docker Desktop. Deferred statements after `defer pool.Close()` do not execute, causing the application to hang. The issue occurs without actual database connections. The problem is demonstrated in a Go program using `pgxpool` with a custom `AfterConnect` function and a failing `aCallWhichFails()` call that returns "test". No other environments have been tested.

documents.title: Why not sync.Pool
documents.summary: Asks why `sync.Pool` should not be used for a resource pool, acknowledging the question is basic.

documents.title: doc: explain differences between puddle and Go sync.Pool
documents.summary: Explains the differences between puddle and Go sync.Pool; addresses issue #38.

documents.title: Feature CreateResource()
documents.summary: CreateResource constructs a new resource without acquiring it and places it directly into the IdlePool without checking the maxSize limit. This feature helps maintain warm resources under low load conditions.

documents.title: Unsafe to bits
documents.summary: Removes the last usage of `unsafe` in the package, replacing a custom log2 implementation in `acquireSemAll` with `bits.Len64`. A panic is proposed as a response if the input number is not greater than zero, since the method is internal and expects a positive value. This change addresses issue #36.

documents.title: WIP: tracing
documents.summary: Proposes a WIP on tracing using `tracerSpan` with defer for ergonomic benefits; considers whether `AcquireStartData` should include only start time or just `AcquireEnd`; notes the use of a big interface, which is not solid, and questions the need for splitting it into subsets; suggests benchmarking; seeks feedback, especially from @jackc, who has three years of experience with the technique.

documents.title: `govulncheck` reports error
documents.summary: `govulncheck` reported an internal error due to an import of "golang.org/x/sync/semaphore" without types, originating from "github.com/jackc/puddle/v2".

documents.title: docs: fix ErrClosedPool wording and small godoc typos
documents.summary: Fixed godoc typos and wording in `pool.go`: changed `ErrClosedPool` from describing a "connection" pool to a "resource" pool; corrected `ReleaseUnused` from "last used used" to "last used"; changed `IdleDuration` from "subtracting … to" to "from"; fixed panic string in `acquireSemAll` from "aquire" to "acquire". Test plan included `go test ./...`; no docs-only behavior changes.

documents.title: fix: nil Pool.Acquire returns error
documents.summary: A nil Pool.Acquire call returns an error with the message "puddle: nil Pool". The code example shows a nil pointer to a *puddle.Pool[int] being used with Acquire(ctx), which causes a panic. The fix is to return a specific error when the Pool is nil instead of panicking.

documents.title: fix: return error from NewPool when config is nil
documents.summary: Changes `NewPool` to return an error when given a nil config instead of panicking, as a nil config is considered a caller mistake that should fail cleanly. The change is tested with `TestNewPoolNilConfig`.

documents.title: Acquire: a released resource stays unusable for as long as the releasing goroutine keeps running (~1 ms per contended acquire)
documents.summary: A released resource remains unusable for ~1 ms per contended acquire due to FIFO handoff in `acquireSem` after `Release`, causing throughput to drop by a third. The issue was first observed in pgxpool v5.10.0 with 200 workers and 4 connections, showing ~1.1 ms idle token time. Benchmarks on Go 1.26.7, puddle v2.2.2, show residue-µs increasing with post-release work (e.g., 335 µs at 1ms work). Fixes include `runtime.Gosched()` after `Release`, a barging fast path, or documenting the behavior. The yield in pgxpool code mitigates the issue.

documents.title: Yield the releasing goroutine's P to a blocked acquirer
documents.summary: Fixes issue #46 by adding `runtime.Gosched()` after semaphore release in `Release`, `Destroy`, and `Hijack` functions, only when a goroutine is blocked in `Acquire`. This yields the releasing goroutine's P to a blocked acquirer, reducing CPU usage. Benchmarks show performance improvement: on linux/arm64 with Go 1.26.7, latency drops from 411–477 µs/op to 255–256 µs/op; on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1, from 411–477 µs/op to 254 µs/op. The fix applies only to contended paths; `CreateResource` and `initResourceValue` are unchanged. A `go vet` warning exists but is not addressed.

documents.title: Destroy background resources invalidated by Close or Reset
documents.summary: Fixes background resource destruction invalidated by Close or Reset; checks closed state and reset generation before adding resources to idle pool. Prevents `Close` from waiting forever and avoids stale resources after `Reset`. Two new tests verify construction synchronization, destruction waiting, and fresh resource creation post-`Reset`. Tests fail before fix; pass after fix. `go test -v -race ./...` passes on Go 1.19, 1.20, 1.23.4; regressions pass 50 race runs. `go vet` finds a benchmark calling `testing.B.Fatal` from a goroutine, present in upstream.

documents.title: Release 1.1.2?
documents.summary: Asks if a new release (version 1.1.2) can be made with the fixes applied.

documents.title: Clarify the meanings of Stats accessors
Ensure that conditional variable is signaled if resource failed to cr…
documents.summary: Ensure that a conditional variable is signaled when a resource fails to create. In a scenario with two goroutines (X and Y) awaiting a resource, if goroutine X fails to create a resource after being triggered by a signal, goroutine Y should be signaled instead of remaining blocked indefinitely. The expected outcome is that goroutine Y will be notified and attempt to create a new resource.

documents.title: Deadlock in CreateResource if pool was closed during resource acquisition
documents.summary: A deadlock occurs in CreateResource when the pool is closed during resource acquisition. The issue arises because the lock on `p.cond.L` is not released after checking `p.closed` and returning `ErrClosedPool`. The repro case shows a test function that closes the pool during resource creation, leading to a deadlock. The error is triggered when `pool.Close()` is called inside the resource creation function. The example is available at https://play.golang.org/p/EaWMf76kzLk.

documents.title: Fix deadlock in Pool.CreateResource
documents.summary: Fixes a deadlock in Pool.CreateResource; details are available in #8.

documents.title: Generics
documents.summary: Inquires whether there is a work in progress on using generics, specifically in the context of anacrolix/torrent, where heap allocation overhead is caused by using google/btree's Item interface. The user expresses willingness to test generics in that repository to reduce allocation overhead.

documents.title: ADMIN
documents.summary: Lists an incomplete task item labeled "____New on here" with a checkmark missing, indicating a pending or unassigned action. No specific decisions, actions, names, dates, or identifiers are provided.

documents.title: The Map[K, V].find() API design discussion
documents.summary: Proposes exporting the Map[K, V].find() method to the public domain by renaming it from find to Find, changing the method signature to accept a key of type K and return index and found status. The method is intended to be used with GetAt(index int) to retrieve a value at a given index. The discussion focuses on API design and visibility of the method.

documents.title: With go1.18rc1 getting error: constraints: package constraints is not in GOROOT
documents.summary: Error occurs when using go1.18rc1 with go get github.com/tidwall/btree@generics; the error states that the package "constraints" is not in GOROOT, specifically located at /Users/<username>/sdk/go1.18rc1/src/constraints. The issue arises during the import of constraints, which is part of the btree package's dependency.

documents.title: Seek does not initialize iter item
documents.summary: `Seek()` does not initialize the iterator's internal item field even when it finds an item, causing `Item()` to return a zero value for the first item. The issue is demonstrated in a Go program using `github.com/tidwall/btree` where `Seek("b")` returns `true` but `iter.Item()` outputs `c`, `d`, and `e` instead of the expected `b`, `c`, `d`, `e`. The bug occurs in Go 1.18rc1 on linux/amd64. The reproduction uses a module named `repro` with a Go version of 1.18.

documents.title: MapIter[K,V] Seek method does not initialize the item
documents.summary: The MapIter[K,V] Seek method fails to initialize the item internally when it returns true, indicating a match or item greater than or equal to the key. As a result, subsequent calls to Item() return the zero value because the item is not properly set.

documents.title: Documentation for Get() is inaccurate
documents.summary: Documentation for Get() incorrectly states Get(key, value) when it should be Get(key); the author offers to submit a pull request if they can resolve the issue and expresses that the b-tree is currently under high usage.

documents.title: Use of interface{} and constant type/length keys
documents.summary: Asks whether the library uses interface{} or adjusts to constant 32-byte binary keys, and expresses concern about potential overhead when using constant-size keys.

documents.title: Breaking changes in switching from uint64 to atomic.Uint64
documents.summary: Using Go version <1.19 causes a compiler error when using atomic.Uint64 due to undefined symbol; the package requires Go 1.19 or later. The issue was found in buntDB, which lacks a Go 1.19 requirement in its go.mod file. The document recommends updating to Go 1.19 in go.mod and explicitly notifying users that the package is not backward compatible.

documents.title: Does btree.Map use concurrency locks?
documents.summary: Asks whether btree.Map uses concurrency locks, noting that NewMap lacks an option to enable or disable locks unlike btree.New.

documents.title: Investigate if we can re-use allocated memory after `Map.Clear()`
documents.summary: Proposes investigating whether allocated memory in btree.Map can be reused after `Map.Clear()` by introducing a `MapNodeMemoryPool` field to store and reuse map nodes. This would allow memory re-use, reduce reallocation needs, and avoid cross-thread dependencies. The suggestion is framed as a potential complexity tradeoff and seeks feedback on whether it is deemed undesirable.

documents.title: How does copy-on-write actually work?
Map for pre-generics version of Go
documents.summary: Asks why there is no map for non-generic versions of Go.

documents.title: possible panic when writing from multiple goroutines
documents.summary: A Go program using the tidwall/btree library panics when writing to a btree.Map from multiple goroutines. The panic occurs at index out of range [9] with length 9 in the nodeSet function of map.go, line 234. The issue arises during concurrent Set operations with 1000 goroutines, each performing 1,000,000 insertions. The code uses rand.Intn(100_000_000_000) to generate keys and calls s.Set(key, j) without synchronization. The panic happens in version v1.6.0 of the btree library.

documents.title: is b+ tree  surport?
documents.summary: Asks whether B+ tree support is available; the document mentions "b++" and "b plus tree" as possible variations or references.

documents.title: add  put method to set kvpairs , if old value exists,  return val
documents.summary: Proposes adding a put method to set key-value pairs that returns the old value if it exists. Notes that a position can hold only one element; if an element is returned to the user, the position becomes available for another element. Therefore, users must retrieve the position status to determine if it is currently in use.

documents.title: Do we need a rebalancing process for the btree?
documents.summary: Asks whether a rebalancing process is needed for the btree and if the tree can grow imbalanced, inquiring about management strategies if imbalance occurs.

documents.title: question about crash during iteration (probably because of mutation during iteration)
documents.summary: Reports a crash during iteration in a Go program using the tidwall/btree library due to mutation (m.Set) during iteration. The crash occurs when calling Next() on a btree.Map iterator after modifying the map. The issue is in a single-threaded application at line 384 of bucket/bucket.go. The user questions whether mutation during iteration is supported, noting that Set() does not update the iterator's internal stack. The user asks if this limitation is documented and offers to submit a PR to add documentation.

documents.title: PathHint on Map/Set?
documents.summary: Asks whether there is a reason Hinting is not exposed on Map and Set, or if it is worth exploring via a PR.

documents.title: Set.GetAt(index int) is `int` sufficient for `index` ?
documents.summary: The document asks whether using `int` for the `index` parameter in `Set.GetAt(index int)` is sufficient, noting that on 32-bit machines, `int` maxes out at 2147483647, which is insufficient for a `uint64`-based set storing up to 18446744073709551615 values. It suggests changing the type to `interface{}` to support all number types in extreme cases. The issue is raised as a personal observation, not a decision or action.

documents.title: Compilation of btree.Set example breaks tinygo
documents.summary: Compilation of the btree.Set example from the README.md fails with a crash when built using `tinygo build -target wasi -o test.wasm`, producing a stack trace from LLVM 18.1. The issue is reported to the tinygo and llvm projects, indicating a bug in the WebAssembly instruction selection phase during code generation. The crash occurs while processing a function in the btree.Map nodeSet method, specifically during debug info resolution in the SelectionDAGBuilder.

documents.title: `IterG`.`Prev` returns true after iterating beyond the end of the tree
documents.summary: The `IterG`.`Prev` method returns `true` after iterating beyond the end of the tree when `Last` is called, followed by `Next`, and then `Prev` is called beyond the far end. This behavior is inconsistent with expectations and causes `Prev` to return `true` even when at the start of the tree. The issue is demonstrated in a test case using `btree.NewBTreeG` with a comparator function, running on Go 1.22.6 on linux/amd64. The bug only surfaces with a `Next` call after `Last`, and the test shows repeated `true` returns beyond the start of the tree.

documents.title: DeleteHint() equal to Delete(), intentional?
documents.summary: Questions whether DeleteHint() in btree.go intentionally ignores the hint parameter by passing nil instead of the provided hint, as it behaves identically to Delete(). The method is noted to return the deleted value or nil if the key was not found, and the user expresses uncertainty about the purpose of hints if they are not used. The code snippet shows the method call passing nil to DeleteHint, raising concern about whether this is intentional or a mistake.

documents.title: avoid overflow on bsearch
documents.summary: Line 97 of btreeg.go in binary search implementation risks integer overflow due to (low + high) / 2; the Go standard library avoids this using int(uint(i+j) >> 1) at sort/search.go:63. The issue is noted as potentially more common if int is int32. The document identifies the specific line (btreeg.go:97) and file (sort/search.go:63) and suggests the fix is worthwhile despite low likelihood of encountering extremely large trees.

documents.title: What does `Mut` mean in various method names?
documents.summary: Asks about the meaning of `Mut` in method names like `IterMut`, `GetMut`, and `ScanMut`. Proposes interpretations: "mutate" (rejected due to absence of `SetMut`), "mutually exclusive" (suggests write locks prevent others from reading), and "mutate current iterated item in place" (changes item contents but not structure). Notes that `Set` automatically obtains a write lock, implying `Mut` may relate to exclusive access rather than mutation.

documents.title: future Go standard mapping APIs
documents.summary: The Go working group for collections is finalizing proposals for standard APIs for hash and tree maps. A draft interface definition at https://go.dev/cl/761460 outlines _AbstractCollection and _AbstractMap interfaces, which model collections and mappings with methods like Clear, Contains, All, At, Delete, Set, Keys, and Values. These interfaces are currently internal and intended to guide future API design for collection datatypes, including B-trees.

documents.title: /go/pkg/mod/github.com/tidwall/btree@v1.8.1/map.go:141 panic: runtime error: index out of range [33] with length 31
documents.summary: A panic occurs in `github.com/tidwall/btree@v1.8.1/map.go:141` during a parallel test when calling `(*btree.Map[string, Address]).Get(key)`, due to index out of range [33] with length 31. The error arises in the `search` function where `low` is 34 but `n.items` has length 31. The user questions if the library is thread-safe and asks if others have encountered this issue. The error occurs in goroutine 12318610.

documents.title: Nice. Does it come with a disk backed version one?
documents.summary: Asks if a disk-backed version of a btree exists that uses less than 100 bytes for empty database creation, noting current empty db size is 1MB; references github.com/timtadh/fs2/bptree and github.com/timtadh/fs2/fmap.
